findings.text: the headline sentence asserts that every other arm 'trades one measure for the other by at most 1.5 points', which the report's own table contradicts: B Jev buys 6.8 points of specificity for 25.0 points of recall, C Drex 9.8 for 44.3, C Jev 9.3 for 33.2 and E 13.1 for 80.3, and the wording is repeated for the first lead question at line 1968; it makes the alternatives look near-equal to the adopted question at line 1968 and in the landing record when each in fact gives up a quarter to four fifths of its recall

the E2 unit rule at name-check-prototype.py:955 re-implements the capability the repository already owns as name_unit_consistency_check, which parses the name's dimensional head and compares it against the declared unit through the same dimension machinery; the addition wraps unit_dimension but duplicates the higher-level name-versus-unit rule and its expectation table as BASE_UNITS at name-check-prototype.py:916 rather than extending audits.py, so the arm's 1.6 per cent recall measures a homemade subset of an existing check and may understate the deterministic baseline the report calls near-useless

FIG_ARMS omits the always-flag control, so the figure carries no point for an arm the tables score, although the brief asks for one labelled point per arm with its interval; the control sits at specificity 0.0 and the x-limit fixed at line 1661 begins at 0.55, so the point cannot be drawn and the legend names only always pass

the arm palette breaks the repository's colour rules: E is drawn in the muddy brown-orange #b5651d the style guidance excludes, and B-drex #3f8f8f sits on the same teal as E+A #0f7b8a so two unrelated arms are hard to tell apart in the rendered figure

_best_arm is evaluated twice and both results are discarded while the conclusion 'No arm measured here improves on it' is hardcoded prose at line 1827, so a regression that reversed an arm's score would regenerate the same sentence and the gate's string-presence check at verify-report.py:77 would still pass
